mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.1%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 10.0% signals severe labor market distress, which typically triggers a short-term equity sell-off as recessionary fears intensify, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 10.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based demand contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to recessionary pressures.
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS < 400000 and HOUST < 900) fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During the early stages of a recession, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a supply-side shock that typically causes S&P 500 underperformance over the next 60 trading days as economic activity contracts.
failure_condition: In the early-stage recession regime (INDPRO declining for 2 consecutive months), S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) below 400,000 (in millions of dollars) indicates weakening demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the recession deepens.
failure_condition: RSAFS decline (below 400,000) fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in employment (PAYEMS) below 130,000 (thousands) signals severe labor market deterioration, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as recessionary fears mount.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS < 130000.0.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL above 255) and weak consumer spending (RSAFS below 400,000) signals stagflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as central bank policy tightening fears intensify.
failure_condition: The joint signal (CPIAUCSL > 255 and RSAFS < 400000) fails to predict negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During the early stages of a recession, a declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals a supply-side shock that typically causes S&P 500 underperformance over the next 20 trading days as economic activity contracts.
failure_condition: In the early-stage recession regime (INDPRO declining for 2 consecutive months), S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
